main_text.l: dem recte foveant, (quod certissime præstituri sunt)
præsertim cum ad manum sint quæcunque fovere,
& longissime absint quæ flammæ huic, si semel
in incendium erumpat, restinguendæ conducere
possent; & quod multo peßimum est, cum satis
appareat exstingui non posse sine insigni victoris
damno.
Præterea licet merito suspicari possemus, convo-
catione hac vestri parlamenti, quæ eorum consiliis
suggesta fuit qui malum hoc civilis discordiæ in cla-
rissima hac insula sine vestro consensu aut consilio
excitarunt, intendi, ut oleum potius quam aquam
restinguendæ huic flammæ afferatis, & in motuum
horum fervore vobis auxiliatoribus utantur ad cons-
tantissimorum vestrorum amicorum ruinam pro-
curandam; quos illi interim ut hostes suos ulciscen-
tur. Nihilominus tamen bonis omnibus in celeber-
rimo vestro coetu non ingratum futurum speramus,
quod summo animi gaudio & hilaritate profite-
mur ac declaremus, vincula amoris & fraternæ
charitatis inter nos esse mutua, & sibi invicem in
omnibus erga Deum & hominem, principem &
populum officiis usque adeo arcte conjuncta, ut
communes amicos & inimicos necesse sit habea-
mus, seu promiscuam utrique salutem contra ho-
stes exteros defendendo, seu alterutrius privilegia
contra domesticos subversores tuendo, a quibus ma-
ius imminet periculum: nisi ab unica & firma sa-
lutis nostræ regula animus nobis fit defcisccre.
Nam cum ratione situs huius insulæ & unionis
sub uno capite, omnes tanquam in una eademque
domo simus, qua corruente, in ejusdem ruinis pro-
miscue omnes sepeliemur: omnes tanquam in una
eademque navi vehamur, qua naufragium patiente
aut ad infames divisionis scopulos impingente, vix
enatabimus; Æquis animis feratis, quod tempesta-
te adhuc

page.notes: Page is a continuous text page. Running head read as "HISTORIA MOTUUM" (printed as "Historia motuum" in small capitals). Two places are doubtful: "constantissimorum" in the line "ruinam procurandam" is printed "constantissimorum" and "vestrorum amicorum" is a plausible reading; the word "fit defcisccre" near the end of the second paragraph is doubtful, and "unionis" in the third paragraph is read as printed. Several words in the first paragraph are only partly legible due to the scan's gutter shadow on the left edge; "dem" at the start is a fragment of "eadem" cut by the page top. Lines of the third paragraph's last line ("te adhuc") are shown as printed. The printed text reads "motuum" in the running head and body, not expanded.
